title: Factoring a finitely presented algebra through B/J, B smooth, J in IB (square-zero base)
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $\Lambda$ a commutative $R$-algebra and $I\subset R$ an ideal. Assume (1) $I^2=0$ and (2) $\Lambda/I\Lambda$ is a filtered colimit of smooth $R/I$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-smooth-algebras]. Let $A$ be a finitely presented $R$-algebra ($A\cong R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_m)$ as $R$-algebras) and $\varphi:A\to\Lambda$ a homomorphism of $R$-algebras. Then there are a smooth $R$-algebra $B$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], a finitely generated ideal $J\subset B$ with $J\subset IB$ ($IB$ the ideal of $B$ generated by the image of $I$), and homomorphisms of $R$-algebras $\psi:A\to B/J$ and $\chi:B/J\to\Lambda$ with $\chi\circ\psi=\varphi$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07CK (lemma-lift-once, line 1238) and its proof (lines 1255-1303: Lemma Tag 07CI lemma-colimit-standard-smooth, Algebra Proposition 00TN, Algebra Lemma 00DV NAK, Algebra Lemma 00R2 finite-presentation-independent)

proof.text: (Reduction modulo $I$.) Write $A\cong R[y_1,\dots,y_p]/(h_1,\dots,h_q)$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Then $A/IA\cong R[y_1,\dots,y_p]/\bigl((h_1,\dots,h_q)+I\,R[y_1,\dots,y_p]\bigr)\cong(R/I)[y_1,\dots,y_p]/(\bar h_1,\dots,\bar h_q)$, $\bar h_l$ the reduction of $h_l$ modulo $I$, so $A/IA$ is a finitely presented, in particular finite type, $R/I$-algebra. Since $\varphi(IA)\subset I\Lambda$, $\varphi$ induces a homomorphism of $R/I$-algebras $\bar\varphi:A/IA\to\Lambda/I\Lambda$ with $\bar\varphi(a\bmod IA)=\varphi(a)\bmod I\Lambda$. Let $p:\Lambda\to\Lambda/I\Lambda$ be the quotient map.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CK (lemma-lift-once, lines 1255-1303): 'Choose a factorization A/IA -> B-bar -> Lambda/I Lambda' (the reduction modulo I that this presupposes)

proof.text: (Factor through a standard smooth $\bar B$.) By hypothesis (2) and [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-standard-smooth-algebras] (Lemma 07CI, applied to the $R/I$-algebra $\Lambda/I\Lambda$), there are a small filtered category $\mathcal K$, a functor $k\mapsto C_k$ to commutative $R/I$-algebras with every $C_k$ standard smooth over $R/I$ [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra], and $R/I$-algebra maps $\iota_k:C_k\to\Lambda/I\Lambda$ forming a colimit in $R/I$-algebras. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise] (1) the same cocone is a colimit of the underlying diagram of commutative rings. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-algebra-factors-filtered-colimit] (Algebra 00QO) over the ring $R/I$ to $C=(R/I)[y_1,\dots,y_p]/(\bar h_1,\dots,\bar h_q)\cong A/IA$ (Step 1) and $g=\bar\varphi$: there are $k$ and a homomorphism of $R/I$-algebras $\bar\alpha:A/IA\to\bar B:=C_k$ with $\bar\beta\circ\bar\alpha=\bar\varphi$, where $\bar\beta:=\iota_k:\bar B\to\Lambda/I\Lambda$. So $\bar B$ is standard smooth over $R/I$ and $A/IA\xrightarrow{\bar\alpha}\bar B\xrightarrow{\bar\beta}\Lambda/I\Lambda$ is a factorization of $\bar\varphi$ by $R/I$-algebra maps.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CK (lemma-lift-once, lines 1255-1303): 'Choose a factorization A/IA -> B-bar -> Lambda/I Lambda with B-bar standard smooth over R/I; this is possible by assumption and Lemma 07CI (lemma-colimit-standard-smooth)'

proof.text: (A presentation of $\bar B$ over $A/IA$.) A standard smooth presentation of $\bar B$ is in particular a presentation, so $\bar B$ is of finite presentation over $R/I$ [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra, def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], and $A/IA$ is of finite type over $R/I$ (Step 1) [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-over-finite-type-algebra] (Algebra 00F4 (4)) applied to $R/I$, $S'=A/IA$, $S=\bar B$, $\sigma=\bar\alpha$, there are $r,s\ge0$ and $\bar g_1,\dots,\bar g_s\in(A/IA)[t_1,\dots,t_r]$ with $\bar B\cong(A/IA)[t_1,\dots,t_r]/(\bar g_1,\dots,\bar g_s)$ as $A/IA$-algebras; write $\bar t_i\in\bar B$ for the class of $t_i$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CK (lemma-lift-once, lines 1255-1303): 'Write B-bar = A/IA[t_1, ..., t_r]/(g-bar_1, ..., g-bar_s)'

proof.text: (Choice of $\lambda_i$, $g_i$, $\epsilon_{ij}$, $\mu_{ij}$.) Since $p$ is surjective choose $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_r\in\Lambda$ with $p(\lambda_i)=\bar\beta(\bar t_i)$, and choose $g_1,\dots,g_s\in A[t_1,\dots,t_r]$ whose coefficientwise reductions modulo $IA$ are $\bar g_1,\dots,\bar g_s$ (possible as $A\to A/IA$ is surjective). For $g\in A[t_1,\dots,t_r]$ let $\varphi(g)(\lambda)\in\Lambda$ be the value at $t_i=\lambda_i$ of the polynomial obtained by applying $\varphi$ to the coefficients; $g\mapsto\varphi(g)(\lambda)$ is the $A$-algebra map $\mathrm{ev}:A[t]\to\Lambda$, $t_i\mapsto\lambda_i$. Then $p\circ\mathrm{ev}$ and the composite $A[t]\to(A/IA)[t]\to\bar B\xrightarrow{\bar\beta}\Lambda/I\Lambda$ agree: both are ring maps that agree on $A$ (as $p\circ\varphi$ equals $\bar\varphi=\bar\beta\circ\bar\alpha$ composed with $A\to A/IA$) and on each $t_i$ (both give $p(\lambda_i)=\bar\beta(\bar t_i)$). The second kills $g_i$ because $\bar g_i\mapsto0$ in $\bar B$. Hence $\varphi(g_i)(\lambda)\in\ker p=I\Lambda$, so $\varphi(g_i)(\lambda)=\sum_{j}\epsilon_{ij}\mu_{ij}$ for finitely many $\epsilon_{ij}\in I$, $\mu_{ij}\in\Lambda$ ($j=1,\dots,N_i$).

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CK (lemma-lift-once, lines 1255-1303): 'say B-bar -> Lambda/I Lambda maps t_i to the class of lambda_i ... Write phi(g_i)(lambda_1, ..., lambda_r) = sum epsilon_ij mu_ij'

proof.text: (The algebra $A'$ and its map to $\Lambda$.) Put $A'=A[t_1,\dots,t_r,\delta_{ij}]/(g_i-\sum_j\epsilon_{ij}\delta_{ij})_{i=1,\dots,s}$ (variables $\delta_{ij}$, $1\le i\le s$, $1\le j\le N_i$), an $R$-algebra via $R\to A$, with the $R$-algebra map $\iota_A:A\to A'$. The $A$-algebra map $A[t,\delta]\to\Lambda$, $t_i\mapsto\lambda_i$, $\delta_{ij}\mapsto\mu_{ij}$ (coefficients through $\varphi$) sends $g_i-\sum_j\epsilon_{ij}\delta_{ij}$ to $\varphi(g_i)(\lambda)-\sum_j\epsilon_{ij}\mu_{ij}=0$ (Step 4), so it induces a homomorphism of $R$-algebras $\varphi':A'\to\Lambda$ with $\varphi'\circ\iota_A=\varphi$. Moreover $A'$ is of finite presentation over $A$ (finitely many variables and relations) and $A$ is of finite presentation over $R$, so $A'$ is of finite presentation over $R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition] (2).

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CK (lemma-lift-once, lines 1255-1303): 'Define A' = A[t_1, ..., t_r, delta_ij]/(g_i - sum epsilon_ij delta_ij) and consider the map A' -> Lambda, a -> phi(a), t_i -> lambda_i, delta_ij -> mu_ij'

proof.text: ($A'/IA'$ is standard smooth over $R/I$.) Since every $\epsilon_{ij}\in I$, $A'/IA'=A[t,\delta]/\bigl((g_i-\sum_j\epsilon_{ij}\delta_{ij})_i+I\,A[t,\delta]\bigr)=(A/IA)[t,\delta]/(\bar g_1,\dots,\bar g_s)\cong\bigl((A/IA)[t]/(\bar g_1,\dots,\bar g_s)\bigr)[\delta]\cong\bar B[\delta_{ij}]$ (Step 3), an isomorphism of $A/IA$-algebras, hence of $R/I$-algebras. Let $(R/I)[x_1,\dots,x_m]/(e_1,\dots,e_c)\cong\bar B$ be a standard smooth presentation [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra], $\det(\partial e_j/\partial x_i)_{i,j\le c}$ [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative] a unit in $\bar B$. Number the $\delta_{ij}$ as $x_{m+1},\dots,x_n$. Then $\bar B[\delta]\cong(R/I)[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(e_1,\dots,e_c)$, and since $e_j$ does not involve $x_{m+1},\dots,x_n$ the matrix $(\partial e_j/\partial x_i)_{i,j\le c}$ is unchanged and its determinant is still a unit (its image under $\bar B\to\bar B[\delta]$). So with $\bar f_j:=e_j$ we have a standard smooth presentation $A'/IA'\cong(R/I)[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(\bar f_1,\dots,\bar f_c)$ with $\bar\Delta:=\det(\partial\bar f_j/\partial x_i)_{i,j=1,\dots,c}$ invertible in $A'/IA'$; write $\bar\xi_i\in A'/IA'$ for the image of $x_i$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CK (lemma-lift-once, lines 1255-1303): 'We have A'/IA' = A/IA[t_1, ..., t_r]/(g-bar_1, ..., g-bar_s)[delta_ij] = B-bar[delta_ij]. This is a standard smooth algebra over R/I as B-bar is standard smooth. Choose a presentation A'/IA' = R/I[x_1, ..., x_n]/(f-bar_1, ..., f-bar_c) with det invertible'

proof.text: (The smooth algebra $B$.) Choose lifts $f_1,\dots,f_c\in R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ of $\bar f_1,\dots,\bar f_c$, let $\Delta=\det(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)_{i,j=1,\dots,c}$ and $B=R[x_1,\dots,x_{n+1}]/(f_1,\dots,f_c,\,x_{n+1}\Delta-1)$. $B$ is standard smooth over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra]: order the variables as $x_1,\dots,x_c,x_{n+1},x_{c+1},\dots,x_n$ and take the $c+1$ equations $f_1,\dots,f_c,x_{n+1}\Delta-1$. Since no $f_j$ involves $x_{n+1}$ and $\partial(x_{n+1}\Delta-1)/\partial x_{n+1}=\Delta$, the $(c+1)\times(c+1)$ matrix of partial derivatives [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative] of these equations with respect to $x_1,\dots,x_c,x_{n+1}$ is block triangular with diagonal blocks $(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)_{i,j\le c}$ and $(\Delta)$, so its determinant is $\Delta^2$, a unit in $B$ because $x_{n+1}\Delta=1$ in $B$. Hence $B$ is a smooth $R$-algebra by [lem-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-is-smooth] (Algebra 00T7 (1)).

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CK (lemma-lift-once, lines 1255-1303): 'Choose lifts f_1, ..., f_c in R[x_1, ..., x_n] ... Then B = R[x_1, ..., x_{n+1}]/(f_1, ..., f_c, x_{n+1} det - 1) is smooth over R' (the standard smooth presentation and the determinant Delta^2 written out)

proof.text: ($B/IB\cong A'/IA'$.) Reduction modulo $I$ is a ring map $R[x]\to(R/I)[x]$ commuting with $\partial/\partial x_i$ and with determinants, so $\Delta$ reduces to $\bar\Delta$ and $B/IB\cong(R/I)[x_1,\dots,x_{n+1}]/(\bar f_1,\dots,\bar f_c,x_{n+1}\bar\Delta-1)$. Define $\bar\theta:B/IB\to A'/IA'$ as the $R/I$-algebra map with $x_i\mapsto\bar\xi_i$ ($i\le n$) and $x_{n+1}\mapsto(\text{image of }\bar\Delta)^{-1}$ (well defined: it kills $\bar f_j$ and $x_{n+1}\bar\Delta-1$), and $\bar\kappa:A'/IA'\cong(R/I)[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(\bar f_j)\to B/IB$, $\bar\xi_i\mapsto x_i$. Then $\bar\theta\bar\kappa=\mathrm{id}$ (check on $\bar\xi_i$) and $\bar\kappa\bar\theta=\mathrm{id}$ (check on $x_i$, $i\le n$, and on $x_{n+1}$: $\bar\kappa(\bar\Delta^{-1})$ is the inverse of $\bar\Delta$ in $B/IB$, which is $x_{n+1}$). So $\bar\theta$ is an isomorphism of $R/I$-algebras. Let $\gamma:B\to A'/IA'$ be $\bar\theta$ composed with $B\to B/IB$; it is a homomorphism of $R$-algebras.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CK (lemma-lift-once, lines 1255-1303): 'there exists an R-algebra map B -> A' which is an isomorphism modulo I' (the isomorphism B/IB = A'/IA' that this presupposes, written out)

proof.text: (Lifting to $\theta:B\to A'$.) Let $q:A'\to A'/IA'$ be the quotient map; its kernel $N=IA'$ satisfies $N^2=I^2A'=0$ by hypothesis (1). Since $B$ is smooth over $R$ (Step 7), [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-square-zero-lifting] (smooth ring maps are formally smooth: Algebra 00TN, via 031J) applied to $R\to B$, $D=A'$, $N$ and $g=\gamma$ gives a homomorphism of $R$-algebras $\theta:B\to A'$ with $q\circ\theta=\gamma$. As $\theta(IB)\subset IA'$, $\theta$ induces $B/IB\to A'/IA'$, which equals $\bar\theta$ (both composed with $B\to B/IB$ give $\gamma$); so $\theta$ is an isomorphism modulo $I$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CK (lemma-lift-once, lines 1255-1303): 'Since smooth ring maps are formally smooth (Algebra, Proposition 00TN) there exists an R-algebra map B -> A' which is an isomorphism modulo I'

proof.text: ($\theta$ is surjective.) View $\theta$ as a homomorphism of $R$-modules $B\to A'$. The induced map $B/IB\to A'/IA'$ is $\bar\theta$, surjective (Step 8), and $I$ is nilpotent ($I^2=0$). By [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-nilpotent] (Algebra 00DV), $\theta$ is surjective.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CK (lemma-lift-once, lines 1255-1303): 'Then B -> A' is surjective by Nakayama's lemma (Algebra, Lemma 00DV)'

proof.text: (The ideal $J$.) Let $J=\ker\theta$. (a) $J\subset IB$: for $b\in J$, $\bar\theta(b\bmod IB)=q(\theta(b))=0$, and $\bar\theta$ is injective (Step 8), so $b\in IB$. (b) $J$ is finitely generated: let $\pi:R[x_1,\dots,x_{n+1}]\to B$ be the quotient map. Then $\theta\circ\pi$ is a surjective homomorphism of $R$-algebras (Step 10) onto $A'$, which is of finite presentation over $R$ (Step 5), so $\ker(\theta\circ\pi)$ is generated by finitely many $P_1,\dots,P_m$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-surjection-kernel-fg] (Algebra 00R2). Since $\pi$ is surjective, $J=\pi(\ker(\theta\circ\pi))$ (if $\theta(b)=0$ write $b=\pi(P)$; then $P\in\ker(\theta\circ\pi)$), so $J$ is generated by $\pi(P_1),\dots,\pi(P_m)$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CK (lemma-lift-once, lines 1255-1303): 'Thus A' = B/J with J in IB finitely generated (see Algebra, Lemma 00R2)'

proof.text: (Conclusion.) By Step 10, $\theta$ induces an isomorphism of $R$-algebras $\tilde\theta:B/J\xrightarrow{\sim}A'$. Put $\psi=\tilde\theta^{-1}\circ\iota_A:A\to B/J$ and $\chi=\varphi'\circ\tilde\theta:B/J\to\Lambda$, homomorphisms of $R$-algebras. Then $\chi\circ\psi=\varphi'\circ\iota_A=\varphi$ (Step 5). With $B$ smooth over $R$ (Step 7) and $J\subset IB$ finitely generated (Step 11) this is the assertion.
